approach: Write Newton's second law for each ball with the same air-resistance force but different mass, and compare their net downward accelerations.

steps.text: Both balls feel the same downward gravity and the same upward air-resistance force, since they are the same size.
steps.equation: m_A a_A = m_A g − F_air, m_B a_B = m_B g − F_air

steps.text: Solve each equation for the net downward acceleration.
steps.equation: a_A = g − F_air/m_A, a_B = g − F_air/m_B

steps.text: Since the mass of A is greater, the same F_air divided by the larger mass subtracts less from g.
The heavier ball A has the larger net downward acceleration, so starting together from the same point it falls faster and reaches the ground first.

common_mistakes.text: Applying the no-air rule that all falling bodies land together regardless of mass, missing that the given equal air-resistance force actually slows the lighter ball more.
